extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) handling Continued Prosecution Applications (CPAs)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner/practitioner procedures for filing, processing, and handling Continued Prosecution Applications (CPAs) under 37 CFR 1.53(d), including eligibility, signatures, fees, filing date rules, treatment of new matter, inventorship, and related form-paragraph notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to disregard CPA and treat as 1.53(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant wants the USPTO to disregard a previously filed request for a CPA filed in a design application (and not recognize its inherent request to expressly abandon the prior application) and to treat the paper as the filing of an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the 1.182 petition expeditiously — the petition will not be granted once the request for a CPA has been entered into the prior application and the inherent request to expressly abandon the prior application has been acknowledged. If the CPA request has been entered by the time the petition and application file are before the deciding official, the petition will be denied. Alternative way to achieve filing a second continuation/divisional without losing benefit: (A) continue prosecution of the original application via the CPA; and (B) file a new continuation/divisional under 37 CFR 1.53(b) claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 during the pendency of the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in CPA; CIP unavailable under CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Since no new matter may be introduced in a CPA, the procedure set forth in 37 CFR 1.53(d) is not available for filing a continuation-in-part application. All continuation-in-part applications must be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) and a newly executed oath or declaration is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any attempt to introduce subject matter not present in the original disclosure will be treated as new matter and is prohibited in a CPA. Use 1.53(b) for CIPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior application's file wrapper and amendments form
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CPA procedure, the continuation or divisional application will utilize the file wrapper and contents of the prior nonprovisional application, including the specification, drawings, and oath or declaration application, and will be assigned the same application number as the prior nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any changes desired when filing the CPA must be made in the form of an amendment to the prior application as it existed prior to filing the CPA (see 37 CFR 1.53(d)(5)). A new specification filed with the CPA request is treated as a substitute specification under 37 CFR 1.125 and is not automatically part of the original application papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute specification and preliminary amendment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new specification filed with the CPA request will not be considered part of the original application papers, but will be treated as a substitute specification in accordance with 37 CFR 1.125; any substitute specification must comply with 37 CFR 1.125(b) (including a statement that the substitute specification includes no new matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification containing new matter will be denied entry by the substitute specification or preliminary examiner. Preliminary amendments (other than substitute specifications) filed with a CPA request will ordinarily be entered, but any new matter entered must be canceled pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 132 from the descriptive portion of the specification, and any claim relying on such new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a). Applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to have the amendment removed from the CPA file and accorded status as a separate application (new file wrapper and application number), but a refund of the CPA filing fee is not available as a result.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA chaining and pendency limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA may be based on a prior CPA so long as the prior CPA is complete under 37 CFR 1.51(b) (except for the inventor’s oath or declaration if the prior CPA contained an application data sheet) and is a design application. There is no other limit to the number of CPAs that may be filed in a chain of continuing applications. However, only one CPA may be pending at one time based on the same prior nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the prior CPA meets completeness requirements; track pendency so only one CPA is pending on the same prior nonprovisional at a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required parts and fees for CPA (including oath/declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.53(d), the specification, claims, drawings, and any amendments entered in the prior nonprovisional application are used in the CPA. A new basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee are required in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 41 and 37 CFR 1.16. The statutory requirement under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is a signed oath or declaration; the previously filed oath or declaration (if any) will be considered to be the oath or declaration of the CPA. For CPAs filed on or after September 16, 2012, the oath or declaration must comply with the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 115 as revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of historic fee rules (no search/exam fees required before Dec 8, 2004) and that a CPA will not be placed on the files for examination until all required parts and fees (including any surcharge) are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original disclosure and new matter carryover
rubrics_metrics.description: The original disclosure of a CPA is the same as the original disclosure of the parent non-continued prosecution application and amendments entered in the parent application(s). Any subject matter added by amendment in the parent application which is deemed to be new matter in the parent application will also be considered new matter in the CPA. No amendment filed in a CPA may include new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims or specification portions that were not properly entered in the parent (or that were new matter in the parent) will be treated as new matter in the CPA and can give rise to rejections/cancellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation consequences: CPA vs RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If application papers for a design application are in any way designated as a CPA filing under 37 CFR 1.53(d), the application papers will be treated by the Office as a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), even if the papers also contain other inconsistent designations. If application papers for a utility or plant application are in any way designated as a CPA filing under 37 CFR 1.53(d), the application papers will be treated as a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct designations; mis-designation can change treatment (e.g., design CPA vs utility RCE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for filing a CPA (eligibility and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application may be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) if the prior nonprovisional application is a design application (not an international design application) that is complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b). If the CPA is filed on or after September 16, 2012, the inventor’s oath or declaration is not required to have been filed in the prior application if the prior application contains an application data sheet indicating inventor information; the inventor’s oath or declaration must be submitted no later than payment of the issue fee. A CPA must be filed before the earliest of: (A) payment of the issue fee on the prior application (unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c) is granted), (B) abandonment of the prior application, or (C) termination of proceedings on the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 37 CFR 1.114 is not available in design applications. Timely filing is critical — CPAs filed after these events are improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing verification checks by Technology Center (TC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA request will be initially processed by the TC assigned the prior application. The TC will verify that (A) the prior application is a design application (not international), (B) the correct prior application number is identified in the request, (C) the request is properly signed, (D) the prior nonprovisional application was pending on, and the issue fee has not been paid on or prior to, the filing date of the CPA request, (E) the prior nonprovisional application was complete under 37 CFR 1.51(b) (with limited exception for oath if ADS present), and (F) the proper filing fee has been paid in the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more conditions are not satisfied or fees are missing, applicant will be notified and no examination will occur until corrected (see 37 CFR 1.53(h)). If an improper or incomplete CPA was processed as proper in error, notify a Legal Instrument Examiner to reprocess and correct records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect prior application number handling and resubmission preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a paper requesting a CPA does not properly identify the prior nonprovisional application number, the TC should attempt to identify the proper application number from other identifying information. If unable to identify, the practitioner may be requested to supply a signed letter providing the correct application number. If all attempts fail, the paper requesting the CPA should be returned to the sender (where a return address exists). If resubmitted with the correct application number within two weeks of the cover letter mail date, the original date of receipt will be considered the CPA filing date (see 37 CFR 1.5(a)). The two-week period to resubmit is not extendible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may use Certificate of Mailing (37 CFR 1.8) or Priority Mail Express (37 CFR 1.10) for resubmissions to preserve date of deposit. If not resubmitted within two weeks, later receipt/deposit date is the filing date. Applicants are urged to include title, applicant name(s), and correspondence address in the CPA request per 37 CFR 1.53(d)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements and consequences for CPA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA is a request to expressly abandon the prior application and therefore must be properly signed. A CPA request filed on or after September 16, 2012, must be signed by: (1) a patent practitioner of record appointed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.32(b); (2) a patent practitioner not of record acting under 37 CFR 1.34; or (3) the applicant (37 CFR 1.42). Unless otherwise specified, papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity must be signed by a patent practitioner. Prior to September 16, 2012, additional signatories (e.g., assignees) were allowed under conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a joint application with no attorney/agent, all applicants must sign the CPA request (unless one applicant is appointed to represent all). An unsigned or improperly signed CPA will be placed in the file of the prior application and is entitled to an application filing date but is ineffective to abandon the prior application and will NOT be examined until properly signed. Correspondence will be sent to the prior application's correspondence address until a new power of attorney or change of correspondence signed by an attorney/agent is filed in the CPA. Pre-2012 assignee signature rules require proof of ownership if relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules and permitted filing methods (EFS, mail, fax, hand delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a CPA is the date on which a request for a CPA on a separate paper for a CPA is filed. A request for a CPA cannot be submitted as part of papers filed for another purpose. CPA requests may be filed via the USPTO electronic filing system (filed as follow-on documents by registered e-filers), by mail, facsimile, or hand delivery. The date of receipt for EFS filings is the date the complete request is received by the Office. Facsimile receipt date rules and weekend/holiday adjustments follow 37 CFR 1.6(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing by facsimile, include required fee authorization (PTO-2038) or application will be treated as filed without fees. 37 CFR 1.6(f) governs evidentiary showing when Office has no evidence of receipt of a faxed CPA. The Certificate of Mailing (37 CFR 1.8) generally does not apply to initial CPA filings (except resubmissions of returned CPA requests). Examples in the MPEP show how receipt dates affect whether a CPA is timely relative to abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee payment, carryover authorizations, insufficiency and surcharge rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing fees for a CPA are the basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(b)), search fee (1.16(l)), and examination fee (1.16(p)). A general authorization to charge fees to a deposit account filed in the prior application carries over to the CPA. If fees are insufficient or omitted after a filing date has been assigned, the applicant will be notified and given time (usually 2 months) to file missing fees and pay the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) to prevent abandonment. CPA will not be examined until all required parts and fees (including any surcharge) are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special surcharge rules vary by filing date ranges (detailed in MPEP): e.g., CPAs filed between Dec 8, 2004 and July 1, 2005 had different surcharge rules than CPAs filed on or after July 1, 2005. For CPAs filed on or after Sep 16, 2012, if the prior application does not contain the inventor’s oath/declaration, a surcharge under 1.16(f) is required unless the oath/declaration is being filed with the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity and micro entity status must be reasserted
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entity status established in the parent application does not automatically carry over to a CPA. Status as a small entity must be specifically established in every application in which it is desired (37 CFR 1.27(c)(4)). Similarly, refiling as a continuation/divisional/CPA requires a new certification of entitlement to micro entity status (37 CFR 1.29(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the CPA request specifically indicates small/micro entity status or includes an assertion, the regular undiscounted filing fee should be charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time and continuity between prior application and CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extension of time is necessary to establish continuity between the prior application and the CPA, the petition for extension of time should be filed as a separate paper directed to the prior nonprovisional application. The separate paper requirement of 37 CFR 1.53(d)(2) is intended to preclude burying a request for a CPA in a paper submitted primarily for another purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CPA is considered a 'reply' for purposes of 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3); an authorization in the prior application to charge fees will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time for continuity. If an extension is filed as a separate paper and the benefits of mailing rules are desired, it must be accompanied by its own certificate of mailing (37 CFR 1.8) or Priority Mail Express (37 CFR 1.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of CPA filing and examiner form-paragraph use
rubrics_metrics.description: Since a 'Notice of Abandonment' is not mailed in the prior application as a result of filing a CPA nor is a filing receipt normally mailed for a CPA, the examiner should advise the applicant that a request for a CPA has been granted by including form paragraph 2.30 in the first Office action of the CPA. Conditional requests will be treated as unconditional and appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 2.35) should be used. If a CPA request was not on a separate paper, use form paragraph 2.31 to notify applicant that no CPA has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified form paragraphs in the first Office action to communicate CPA status, filing date, and consequences (see para text and examiner notes for 2.30, 2.35, 2.31). If a conditional request was treated as unconditional, advise applicant accordingly because abandonment of the parent may have occurred by operation of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship carryover and procedure to change inventive entity
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventive entity set forth in the prior nonprovisional application automatically carries over into the CPA unless the request for a CPA is accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of the name(s) of person(s) who are not inventors of the invention being claimed in the CPA (37 CFR 1.53(d)(4)). The statement requesting deletion must be signed by authorized persons (lists differ pre- and post-September 16, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should acknowledge receipt of a deletion statement in the first Office action using form paragraph 2.32 and thereafter send the file to OPAP to revise records. The inventive entity of the CPA is the same as the prior application even if a transmittal letter or new oath names a different inventor; to change the inventive entity as asserted in the CPA, file a request under 37 CFR 1.48 with the required fee (see MPEP § 602.01(c)).
